newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CBA repeats sees flat 96/97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CBA repeats sees flat 96/97 earnings.

text.p: Commonwealth Bank of Australia repeated in its annual report released on Wednesday that it expected flat earnings in the current year to June 30, 1997, but that earnings per share should improve because of the recently completed share-buyback.
CBA Managing Director David Murray said in the report the reduction in home lending margins and other factors would affect earnings and competitiveness in the current year.

"Taking these factors into account, the bank's expectation for 1996/97 is that earnings will be flat, but as a result of completion of the share buy-back approved by shareholders on May 14, earnings per share should improve," Murray said.
CBA said on August 21 when releasing its 1995/96 results that it saw flat earnings in 1996/97 and better earnings per share.
CBA reported a 13.8 percent rise in net profit to A$1.119 billion for 1995/96.
It also repeated that the dividend payout ratio would be maintained in 1996/97, as long as there were no significant changes in the bank's activities.
